items.title: Georg Brunis Interview, 1958-06-03
items.q: They let Palazolo go, and, uh, Tony Palazolo, I think that's his name.

ctx.x: Uh, I think it was the Sydney. The JS? No, the JS was turned into the Sydney. It is. Yeah, that's it. It was the JS. So, uh, Rap Poli got the job. They let Palazolo go, and, uh, Tony Palazolo, I think that's his name. So, uh, Rap joined the band, and then we, that's where I met Black, the banjo player, and, uh, Bix used to come out and, uh, sit in. It was from Davenport, and, well, he was a great trumpet player. God bless him. And, uh, then from the boat, we'd, uh, we got the offer to come into Friars Inn.
Well, can you tell me a little bit about Rap? Had he been, uh, living in Davenport, working on a boat, or what?
